newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to launch new exports financing mechanism.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to launch new exports financing mechanism.

text.p: Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), in a bid to stem surging trade and current account deficits, will implement probably as early as next month new financing mechanisms to promote exports, Planning Minister Antonio Kandir said.
"New instruments will be ready by December or January," Kandir told reporters before a luncheon speech on the second day of the Business Future of the Americas Forum.
He said Brazil would post "significant" monthly trade deficits into 1997, but that exports will be on the rise next year.
"By the middle of 1997, the level of exports should be above the average now," Kandir said.
Reiterating a common government theme these days, he said Brasilia will not tinker with monetary policy to improve the trade picture.
"Our view is that there should be no short-term measures," he said.
Brazil will begin to see the results of export-boosting efforts in early 1997, Kandir said.
Meanwhile, he said the National Privatization Council (CND) will accelerate the pace of the country's privatizations, but he did not elaborate.
